answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use graduated trust built on verifiable work history. New identities start with almost no privileges and earn capability slowly, only after completing attested tasks other agents can check, like a crystal forming layer by layer. Each verified job adds a small non-transferable reputation increment, while one bad act triggers a ripple of distrust that freezes the account's earned standing. Because trust accrues over time and cannot be bought, an attacker must pay the ferrous cost of doing real work thousands of times over, making fake identities pointless.
